### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**1** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them. ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/ui.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/view.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/ui.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/view.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **177** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3f7deed120dd2ec8f34333fc013152c75d7fe3bc` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `5c4e0437c45d605f3b914845e359488ee0c2510b` — the merge of head `cfca0e203fcfac63157b43cdeec7424a18bcb877` into base `3f7deed120dd2ec8f34333fc013152c75d7fe3bc`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 5c4e0437c45d605f3b914845e359488ee0c2510b && git checkout 5c4e0437c45d605f3b914845e359488ee0c2510b
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 3f7deed120dd2ec8f34333fc013152c75d7fe3bc cfca0e203fcfac63157b43cdeec7424a18bcb877 && git checkout -B drift-repro 3f7deed120dd2ec8f34333fc013152c75d7fe3bc && git merge --no-ff cfca0e203fcfac63157b43cdeec7424a18bcb877

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3f7deed120dd2ec8f34333fc013152c75d7fe3bc
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `eb042a64a5bbb7657d896c6c8bd4558e61777ba0`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts + ui/packages/plugin-detail/src/comments/recordCounts.ts, ui/packages/plugin-kanban/src/ObjectKanban.tsx, ui/packages/plugin-kanban/src/KanbanCardDisplay.ts, ui/packages/plugin-kanban/src/KanbanImpl.tsx, ui/packages/plugin-list/src/ListView.tsx, ui/packages/plugin-list/src/components/ViewSettingsPopover.tsx, ui/packages/plugin-view/src/ObjectView.tsx, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/objectViewOptions.ts, packages/spec/liveness/view.json

First round, for card #36423 under ruling 7122246952. Read: the card and its six comments, the PR body and file list, the net diff against `main` (merge base `9a65a48f8`), and the head's check-runs. The rest of the diff (tests, the i18n packs, generated docs and baselines, the changeset) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept set of `KanbanConfigSchema`: one new optional key, `cardFooter`.** It is an inline strict object with two optional booleans, `comments` and `attachments`. Newly accepted: `cardFooter: {}` and either member as `true` or `false`. Still refused: a `cardFooter` that is not an object, a member that is not a boolean, and any other member, by name (`timeInColumn` is the pinned case). The block was already strict, so `cardFooter` was an unknown key on `main`; nothing accepted there is refused here. Right: a widening only.
- **No spec default at either level.** A stored view parses to what it was. Right.
- **Metadata-protocol kind `added`.** A new key an author can write. Right.
- **Public surface, all additive.** `@objectstack/spec` gains no export; the inferred `KanbanConfig` type gains one optional member. `@object-ui/plugin-detail` exports `useRecordCounts`, `recordCountIds`, `compileCommentCountQuery`, `compileAttachmentCountQuery`, `readRecordCounts` and three types. `KanbanCardDisplay` gains optional `footerCounts`; `ViewSettingsKanban` gains two optional toggles. Right.
- **Enforced end to end (ADR-0049).** Both producers of the `object-kanban` node (`ListView`, `ObjectView#generateViewSchema`) and the Console's `kanbanViewOptions` relay the key only when declared; `ObjectKanban` asks a count only for a member that is exactly `true`; `SortableCard` draws it. The `kanban` liveness note agrees with that code sentence by sentence, and the authorable-surface row, the reference page and the strictness counts (one more strict site in `view.zod.ts`) agree with the schema. Right.
- **Check-runs on the head.** None is red; the skipped ones are queue-only, scheduled or opt-in jobs. `TypeScript Type Check` (the spec's generated-artifact gates), `Spec property liveness`, `Check Changeset`, `Type Check UI`, `Test UI`, `Test Core`, `Lint & Repo Gates` and `Governed Surface Queue Guard` are green.

### ② Semver level

The changeset takes `minor` on seven packages, and the diff moves exactly those seven (`@objectstack/spec`, and `plugin-detail`, `plugin-kanban`, `plugin-list`, `plugin-view`, `app-shell`, `i18n` under `@object-ui`). An `added` kind takes at least `minor` on a package the diff moves, so the level is right. The PR body and the changeset both carry the two declaration lines with the same values, `yes (widening)` and `added`; both are true of the diff. Nothing is removed or renamed, so no migration text and no ADR-0087 disposition is owed.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **The counts and the reader's own access.** Each count is a grouped read through the existing data door as the signed-in reader. The read gates of both counted objects cover grouped reads and narrow them to rows whose parent record that reader can read, so a card cannot show a count of rows its reader cannot read. The diff adds no server code and no route, so it cannot widen what a reader can count. A refused read draws nothing. No leak found.
- **SQL push-down.** No server-side read is added. Each count is one `GROUP BY` aggregate in the database, and the access narrowing is composed into that statement. The id list is the cards the board has already loaded, which is what the acceptance names ("one grouped read per counted object over the loaded cards, never one per card"). No id materialisation and no in-app join. No finding.
- **Decision: orphan replies are not counted.** Accepted. A grouped read cannot see whether a row's parent still exists, and the grouped door has no way to ask it. The record page counts such a reply as an open thread that the server refuses to resolve, so the card's number is the one a user can bring to zero. It is a stated difference from the record page; see N1 for where it is not yet stated.
- **Decision: the two toggles are offered by capability.** Accepted. The gates are the record page's own (`enable.feeds` opt-out, `enable.files` opt-in), and the board applies the same two before it asks.
- **The `Skills-docs:` line, `follow-up #37612`.** Acceptable. The claim template prescribes `follow-up #N` for a key taught under `skills/**` on any PR outside `domain:skills`, because that tree is governed. #37612 is open, names the file and the section, and is blocked on this card. The generated reference page carries the key meanwhile. The same route was taken for the previous board settings.
- **Item 2, time in column.** Dropped by the maintainer, 「不需要这个功能」 (7122246952). The diff adds no member for it and pins its refusal. `Fixes #36423` is right on item 1 alone.
- **The unchecked Human Minimum box** (full local suite not run) and the one local red the body names: the head's `Test Core` and `Test UI` are green, so CI answered both.
- **Overlap with #37581, #37422, #37366.** GitHub reports the PR mergeable. The reference page and the strictness counts are generated: whichever lands second regenerates them.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts`, against the ruling and its first consumer. The shape is the one the ruling left to this review, and it holds. It is closed at both levels, with a `surface` of its own for the refusal. It has no default. An object rather than two flat booleans means a later foot item is one more member, refused until a reader draws it. The two `describe` strings state what is shown and that an absent or `false` member is not read, which is what `ObjectKanban` does. `{}` and a `false` member mean the same as absence, as `showFieldLabels: true` does; the view settings write only `true` or remove the member. A member set on an object without the capability parses and is never asked; no such row can exist there, so "a count of zero draws nothing" still holds.

Read to judge the reader, outside the diff: `{ parent_id: null }` is the spec's null test, `{ $ne: true }` is NULL-safe on the SQL driver and is the reader spelling `sys-comment.object.ts` names, and a `count` with an alias and no field is the lane count's own shape. The two compiled reads say what the header says.

No must-fix.

**S1 (should-fix) — a cut answer is drawn as a whole one.** `readRecordCounts` never reads the answer's `hasMore`. The contract of `DataSource.queryGroupHeaders` (`ui/packages/types/src/data.ts`) says a group absent from a partial answer was dropped, not empty, and that a caller reading an absent group as an empty one must check the flag first. The reader's header says a record the answer does not name "has no count, rather than a zero", but `SortableCard` draws a missing count and a zero count the same way: nothing. The door cuts a grouped read that names no `limit` to the deployment's default page size (`OS_DATA_DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE`), and these reads name none. On a deployment that sets it, a board with more counted cards than that page (a lane loads 50) shows no foot on the cards past the cut, in no stated order, while they have open threads or files. The two sibling callers in the tree treat a cut answer as not known (`KanbanLaneStatistic.ts`, `usedCurrencyCodes.ts`). Fix it in the reader so a cut can never pass as zero, for example by asking again over the ids the answer did not name (still grouped, never one per card), and pin it with a `hasMore` answer at the board.

**S2 (should-fix) — the counts are not asked again when a counted row is written.** `reloadKey` in `ObjectKanban` is the board's own refresh, the invalidation nonce of the board's object and the host reload. A comment posted or a thread resolved in the record drawer a card opens (the default navigation mode) writes `sys_comment`; an upload writes `sys_attachment`. Both are announced on the data-invalidation bus under their own object name, which none of the three keys reads. So after the user's own comment the card keeps the old number, or no foot, until something else reloads the board. The reader should also ask again on a write to the object it counts, while that count is asked.

**N1 (nit) — "the number the record page's comments icon shows" has two exceptions, one unstated.** The jsdoc on `cardFooter` and the changeset both say it. The reader's header and the PR body state the first (a reply whose parent was deleted). The second is not stated: the record page reads a record's comments by `thread_id`, the reader by the stamped pair `object_name` and `record_id`, so a comment written before the pair existed is not counted until `os migrate comment-parent-pair --apply` has stamped it. Accepted as a deviation: the pair is the indexed key the read gate narrows by. Name both in the changeset and the PR body; the jsdoc can follow with the next change to that file.

**N2 (nit) — the feet blink when the card set changes.** `useCountRead` returns `null` from the render the question changes until the new answer lands, and the question holds the id list. Loading a lane's next page or creating a card clears every foot on the board for one round trip. A reload over the same ids keeps them. Counts of ids present in both sets are still true and could stay. It can ride the S1 and S2 fix, since that moves the same file.

The other implementing files agree with the contract: `KanbanCardDisplay.ts` and `KanbanImpl.tsx` draw only counts above zero, the three relays pass the key through only when declared, and the two toggles write the member on or gone, with no `cardFooter` left once both are off.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-th9squ`
Reviewed-by: `session_01L6bhgV6i8jfWwSXjpWJrjA`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `6ee3bc414aae53a6c48f6c8338d2d3c847116448`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts + ui/packages/plugin-detail/src/comments/recordCounts.ts, ui/packages/plugin-detail/src/comments/index.ts, ui/packages/plugin-detail/src/index.tsx, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/RecordAttachmentsPanel.tsx, ui/packages/plugin-kanban/src/ObjectKanban.tsx, ui/packages/plugin-kanban/src/KanbanCardDisplay.ts, ui/packages/plugin-kanban/src/KanbanImpl.tsx, ui/packages/plugin-list/src/ListView.tsx, ui/packages/plugin-list/src/components/ViewSettingsPopover.tsx, ui/packages/plugin-view/src/ObjectView.tsx, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/objectViewOptions.ts, packages/spec/liveness/view.json

DELTA review from `eb042a64a5bbb7657d896c6c8bd4558e61777ba0` (record 7202278679: PASS, should-fix S1 and S2, nits N1 and N2) to this head. Read: card #36423 and its six comments, the PR body and file list, the diff between the two heads in full (one commit, eight files) and the net diff against `main`, and the head's check-runs. The rest of the diff (tests, the i18n packs, generated docs and baselines, the changeset) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

- **S1: closed.** `askRecordCounts` reads `hasMore` off the answer as returned and asks again over the records the answer did not name. Pinned in the reader's test and at the board (case e).
- **N1: closed** on the prose faces. The changeset and the PR body name both exceptions, and the reader's header now names the second. The `cardFooter` jsdoc still says "the number the record page's comments icon shows" with neither; that is the deviation round 1 accepted, and no follow-up card carries it yet (see N3).
- **N2: closed.** While a new set of the same object's records is asked, a record in both sets keeps its count. Another object's counts, or a count no longer asked, are not drawn.
- S2 stays open in part; see ④.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept set of `KanbanConfigSchema`: unchanged this round.** The diff between the two heads touches no file under `packages/`. The round-1 judgments stand: a widening only, no spec default, kind `added`.
- **Public surface, additive.** `@object-ui/plugin-detail` exports two more names, `askRecordCounts` and `MAX_COUNT_ROUNDS`, from both entry files. `useRecordCounts` keeps its input and output types. Right.
- **`useRecordCounts` now returns the kept counts, not `null`, while a new set is asked.** The hook is new in this PR, so no shipped caller sees a change. Right.
- **One shipped behaviour moves: `RecordAttachmentsPanel` announces an upload and the uploader's own delete on the client data-invalidation bus.** Before this head neither was announced. Right, and the changeset says so; who hears it is under ③.
- **Check-runs on the head.** 74 runs, none red; the skipped ones are queue-only, scheduled or opt-in jobs. `Test UI`, `Test Core`, `Type Check UI`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Check Changeset`, `Spec property liveness` and `Governed Surface Queue Guard` are green.

### ② Semver level

The changeset's package list is unchanged: `minor` on the same seven packages. This round moves `plugin-detail` (two additive exports), `app-shell` (the panel's two announcements) and a test in `plugin-kanban`; all three are already at `minor`, so the level is right. The two declaration lines are unchanged and still true. The changeset text now states the cut answer, the re-ask on a write, the kept counts and the panel's announcements. It names `askRecordCounts` but not `MAX_COUNT_ROUNDS` or the 20-round bound; the level does not depend on that.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **The re-ask loop ends and cannot spin.** Each round is one grouped read. The loop stops on a whole answer, on a cut answer that names none of the records still asked, when no record is left, or after `MAX_COUNT_ROUNDS` (20). A record counts as named only if it is among those still asked, and every named record leaves the next round's list, so the list shrinks by at least one per round. A server that answers `hasMore` every time, or that ignores the narrowed list and names records no longer asked, is bounded at 20 reads. A read that never answers issues nothing further, and a later ask replaces it.
- **The bound is a stated limit.** Past 20 cut pages a record still unnamed has no count, and the card draws that as it draws zero. With a deployment page of 50 groups that is 1,000 counted cards. Accepted; the reader's header states it.
- **Row access.** Every round rides the same door as the same signed-in reader, with the same filter and a shorter id list. This round adds no server code and no route, so the round-1 reading holds: a card cannot show a count of rows its reader cannot read.
- **What the two new notifications carry, and who hears them.** Each carries the object name `sys_attachment` and the attachment row's id. The bus (`ui/packages/react/src/data-invalidation.ts`) is a listener set inside the page, plus one event dispatched on the same window. Nothing is sent to the server, to another tab or to another user. The listeners are the readers mounted in the writer's own page, and each re-reads through the data door as that same user. The id is one the server had just answered to that user (the upload) or one the user had already listed (the delete). An announcement follows only a write the server admitted. No leak found, and nothing is held back for a private report.
- **What other listeners now see.** Readers of `sys_attachment` in the same page re-read in place: lists and related lists of it, its related-count badges, the verdict caches for that row, a record page that lists it as a child object, and the element-API read cache, which any data change drops. That is what a delete of an attachment through the data door already did. Nothing is remounted or navigated. The changeset states the change, and `@object-ui/app-shell` is at `minor`.
- **SQL push-down.** No server-side read is added. Each round is still one `GROUP BY` in the database with the access narrowing in the statement. The shorter id list is the loaded cards minus the records already named, computed in the browser from ids the board holds. No id materialisation and no in-app join. No finding.
- **The acceptance sentence, "one grouped read per counted object over the loaded cards, never one per card".** On a whole answer it holds to the letter. Over a cut answer the reader takes one grouped read per page of groups, at most 20, never one per card. Accepted as within the route; this is the fix round 1 named. N3 covers the three texts that still say one read without the qualifier.
- **"A comment posted or resolved in the record drawer is announced" (PR body; the reader's header says the same).** True for posted, not for resolved. See S2.
- **Spec untouched, the jsdoc deferred.** Accepted, as round 1 allowed.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts` is byte-identical to the head round 1 judged, and that judgment stands: the shape holds against the ruling and against `ObjectKanban`, its first consumer.

`ui/packages/plugin-detail/src/comments/recordCounts.ts`, sentence by sentence against the tree. The cut-answer paragraph agrees with `askRecordCounts`: `hasMore` is read on the array the adapter returns (`queryGroupHeaders` in `data-objectstack` sets it there), the named records keep their exact count, and a record never named has no entry. The kept-counts logic agrees with its comment. The last paragraph of the header does not agree with the tree, which is S2.

`ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/RecordAttachmentsPanel.tsx` agrees with what the reader relies on. The upload is announced per file after the server answers an attachment id, a refused upload is not, and the own-delete is announced after the removal door answers. The other delete branch goes through the data source, whose mutation event the console bridges to the bus. The rename door moves no count and is rightly silent. No other file in `ui/packages` writes `sys_attachment` past the data source.

No must-fix.

**S2 (should-fix) — still open for the comment doors: resolving or reopening a thread, and a member's delete of their own comment, are not announced, so the card keeps the old number.** The reader now listens for `sys_comment` writes, and a comment posted (`dataSource.create`) reaches it. But the open-thread count moves most directly when a thread is resolved or reopened, and `handleResolveComment` in `ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/RecordDetailView.tsx` writes that through `PUT /api/v1/comments/:id/resolution` with the authenticated fetch, not the data source. `handleDeleteComment` does the same with `DELETE /api/v1/comments/:id` for a caller without the delete grant, which is the ordinary member. Neither calls `notifyDataChanged`, and no bridge covers a raw fetch. So after a user resolves a thread in the drawer a card opens, the card still shows the thread as open until something else reloads the board; closing the drawer does not. This is the case round 1 named ("a thread resolved in the record drawer"). The reader's header and the PR body say a resolved comment is announced; the tree says otherwise. The board's case (f) pins the listener with a hand-made notification, so it cannot see this. Fix it where this round fixed the attachments: announce a `sys_comment` write after each of the two doors answers, and pin each at `RecordDetailView`.

**N3 (nit) — three texts still say one read where the reader may now take several.** The `cardFooter` jsdoc ("in ONE grouped read per counted object") and its `describe` ("each read once for the whole board") in `view.zod.ts`, and the `kanban` liveness note ("in ONE grouped read for the board"), are exact only for a whole answer. No effect on the accept set or on what is drawn. It belongs with the deferred jsdoc change from N1: either take both in the commit that fixes S2 and regenerate the reference page and baselines, or file one follow-up card for both.

**N4 (nit) — an ask that has been replaced keeps reading.** `useCountRead` drops a superseded answer but `askRecordCounts` takes no signal, so over a cut answer its remaining rounds still run. Uploading several files announces each one, and each announcement starts a new ask. Only a deployment that cuts sees more than one wasted read per ask. Left as an accepted deviation unless the S2 commit is in the file anyway.

The other implementing files are unchanged since the head round 1 judged and still agree with the contract.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-th9squ`
Reviewed-by: `session_01L6bhgV6i8jfWwSXjpWJrjA`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `cfca0e203fcfac63157b43cdeec7424a18bcb877`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts + ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/RecordDetailView.tsx, ui/packages/plugin-detail/src/comments/recordCounts.ts, ui/packages/plugin-detail/src/comments/index.ts, ui/packages/plugin-detail/src/index.tsx, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/RecordAttachmentsPanel.tsx, ui/packages/plugin-kanban/src/ObjectKanban.tsx, ui/packages/plugin-kanban/src/KanbanCardDisplay.ts, ui/packages/plugin-kanban/src/KanbanImpl.tsx, ui/packages/plugin-list/src/ListView.tsx, ui/packages/plugin-list/src/components/ViewSettingsPopover.tsx, ui/packages/plugin-view/src/ObjectView.tsx, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/objectViewOptions.ts, packages/spec/liveness/view.json

DELTA review, round 3, from `6ee3bc414aae53a6c48f6c8338d2d3c847116448` (record 7203377375: PASS, carrying S2 and the nits N3 and N4) to this head. Read: card #36423 and its six comments, the PR body and file list, records 7202278679 and 7203377375, the diff between the two heads in full (two commits, seven files), the net diff against `main` (38 files), and the head's check-runs. `RecordDetailView.tsx` joins the implementing files this round. The rest of the diff (tests, the i18n packs, generated docs and baselines, the changeset) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

- **S2: closed.** Resolving or reopening a thread, and a member's delete of their own comment, each announce one `sys_comment` write once the door has answered, and none when the door refuses. Pinned at `RecordDetailView` for both doors, both ways.
- **N3: closed.** The `cardFooter` jsdoc, its `describe` and the `kanban` liveness note now say what the reader does over a cut answer, and the reference page was regenerated to match.
- **N1: closed** in full. The jsdoc now names both exceptions to the record page's number, which round 1 let wait for the next change to that file.
- **N4: closed** as an accepted deviation. The PR body lists it under its decisions and the reader's header states it.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept set of `KanbanConfigSchema`: unchanged this round.** The spec hunk is the `cardFooter` jsdoc and one `describe` string. No schema node, member, default or strictness option moves, so every stored view parses to what it did at the head round 2 judged. Right: description only.
- **Published text.** The `describe` string is the row the generated reference page prints. At this head the page carries the new sentence in its three kanban tables, and no file in the tree still carries the old one.
